comentarios.texto: WHAT: every embed comment/retriever check now does a SELECT via record_for_host instead of the previous in-memory SiteSetting string check. WHY: adds a DB round-trip to the hot unauthenticated embed path on every request, increasing latency and DB load. HOW: cache the host list with expiry and invalidate on EmbeddableHost save/destroy.

hist.text: embed_controller.rb:61 and lib/topic_retriever.rb:16 now call EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?, which runs a SELECT (embeddable_host.rb:17) instead of reading the in-memory SiteSetting. Real, but a single small query per embed request is a micro-optimisation with no meaningful user impact.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 adds a single lookup for the newly database-backed host configuration, but this does not establish a meaningful performance defect. Successful comments responses enable caching at app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:35, and lib/middleware/anonymous_cache.rb:121-122 serves cache hits without invoking the controller, so the lookup does not run on every anonymous request.

Concede. The lookup is the intended consequence of moving hosts to a DB table (embeddable_host.rb:17 `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`), one indexed query, and anonymous GETs are served from Redis by lib/middleware/anonymous_cache.rb:121 `helper.cached or helper.cache(@app.call(env))` once embed_controller sets the cache duration, so the claimed per-request DB round-trip on the hot path does not hold. Nothing worth reporting.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: handler directly instantiates CalendarCacheRepository instead of the calendar-cache.ts factory that returns CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when disabled. WHY: when calendar-cache is disabled it still issues prisma.calendarCache.groupBy and can expose status inconsistent with the rest of the app. HOW: resolve the repository through the existing factory that respects isCalendarCacheEnabledGlobally.

hist.text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of going through CalendarCache.init (calendar-cache.ts:22-29), bypassing the feature-flag check and leaving the PR's own CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds dead. Effect is an extra groupBy and possibly showing stale cache timestamps while the cache is disabled.

connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28-29 directly constructs the repository, whose calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-182 unconditionally queries Prisma. This bypasses calendar-cache.ts:24-28 and the disabled implementation returning [] in calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-29, allowing cache status and actions to remain visible while caching is disabled (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69-107).

Concede. connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 `new CalendarCacheRepository()` bypasses calendar-cache.ts:27-28 (`if (isCalendarCacheEnabledGlobally) ... return new CalendarCacheRepositoryMock()`), and the PR itself added the mock's getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returning [] (calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-29) for the disabled case. With the flag off, leftover rows still yield cacheUpdatedAt and CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69 `hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` shows cache status/actions: user-visible wrong behaviour, not just an extra query.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: fixed /tmp/tmole.log combined with rm -f and shell redirect follows symlinks. WHY: a local attacker pre-creating /tmp/tmole.log as a symlink causes truncation/overwrite of an arbitrary victim-owned file when the script runs. HOW: create the log with mktemp and avoid predictable paths.

hist.text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:4,35-36 does `rm -f /tmp/tmole.log` before redirecting, which removes a pre-planted symlink; exploiting it needs a local attacker winning a race on a developer machine for a local dev helper script, so there is no practical problem to report.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:4 uses a predictable shared temporary path, and lines 34-35 perform an unchecked removal followed by a symlink-following truncating redirect. Although successful removal unlinks an existing symlink, an attacker-owned link can survive a denied removal in sticky /tmp, or be inserted between removal and opening; on systems permitting symlink following, the victim's writable target is truncated.

Concede the class: my premise that `rm -f "$LOG_FILE"` (test-gcal-webhooks.sh:34) always removes a planted symlink is wrong, since in sticky /tmp a link owned by another user cannot be unlinked and rm -f fails silently, then line 35 `tmole $TM_PORT > "$LOG_FILE"` follows it (no fs.protected_symlinks on macOS, the script's target given `sed -i ''` at line 68). Severity medium rather than high: a local-dev helper script, only on shared multi-user hosts.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Switching from interpolateVariablesInQueries to applyTemplateVariables drops the datasource:getRef() assignment. WHY: Old method (datasource.ts:436-438) stamped each query with datasource ref; new method (datasource.ts:1135-1140) returns only expr/step/legendFormat, leaving stale/missing datasource on split targets for downstream routing. HOW: Preserve the datasource ref when mapping, as the old path did.

hist.text: shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52 now uses applyTemplateVariables (datasource.ts:1110-1140), which indeed does not stamp datasource: getRef(); but DataSourceWithBackend.query (packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:149-172) defaults to this.getRef() and resolves q.datasource with scopedVars, so routing is unaffected.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/datasource.ts:1135-1139 spreads ...target, preserving its datasource rather than returning only expr/step/legendFormat. Split requests call datasource.runQuery (querySplitting.ts:180), which delegates to super.query (datasource.ts:350-352); packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:149-186 defaults missing datasource references to this.getRef(), resolves supplied references, and explicitly assigns the outgoing datasource, so the claimed routing failure is unsupported.

Concede. The comment's WHY rests on applyTemplateVariables returning only expr/step/legendFormat, but datasource.ts:1135-1140 returns `{ ...target, expr: exprWithAdHoc, step, legendFormat }`, keeping the target's datasource; DataSourceWithBackend.query also defaults missing refs to this.getRef(). The fact the problem relies on is false, so hallucination; severity as stated (routing of split queries broken) is high.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: canView(user)/canManage(user) dropped ADMIN role from hasOneAdminRole check. WHY: Admins relying on ADMIN role lose view/manage access (denial) diverging from prior contract and V1 behavior. HOW: Restore AdminRoles.ADMIN in the role checks or prove ADMIN is handled elsewhere.

hist.text: MgmtPermissions.hasOneAdminRole (MgmtPermissions.java:163-173) checks client roles of the realm-management/master admin client, where 'admin' is not a client role; admins get manage-users through realm-admin/admin composites. V1 UserPermissions (lines 234, 298) never included AdminRoles.ADMIN, so nothing diverges.

The removal is real, but hasOneAdminRole checks client roles, not the realm-level ADMIN role (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/MgmtPermissions.java:163-173). ADMIN already inherits the management client roles through composites (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/managers/RealmManager.java:346-365), so administrators retain access. The remaining checks also match V1’s manage/view checks (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissions.java:234,298).

Concede the subclass. The removal is real (UserPermissionsV2.java:48 now `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)`), and the comment itself allows that ADMIN may be handled elsewhere; only the inferred impact is wrong, because hasOneAdminRole checks management client roles (MgmtPermissions.java:163-173) that the ADMIN composite already includes (RealmManager.java:346-365). True facts, no problem: FP none.

comentarios.texto: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes FilteredPayload to decoder and expects None to skip+commit. The wired decoder partial(self.decode_payload,...) asserts not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload), so filtered messages raise AssertionError into the generic except instead of the intended None fast-path (error log + reliance on exception fallback). Guard FilteredPayload before delegating to decode_payload.

hist.text: result_consumer.py:188 asserts the payload is not FilteredPayload, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy is the first step returned by create_thread_queue_parallel_worker (lines 245-259) with no upstream filter, so Kafka never delivers FilteredPayload to it; even if it did, the except at queue_consumer.py:317-325 still completes the offset.

src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py:256 wires decode_payload directly, whose assertion at line 188 rejects FilteredPayload. queue_consumer.py:295 invokes that decoder before the None check, causing filtered messages to produce the erroneous exception log at line 318; lines 319–325 still complete their offsets through the fallback.

Keep FP none (raising severity to medium as stated: misleading error log). The assertion mismatch exists, but no FilteredPayload can reach it: create_thread_queue_parallel_worker (result_consumer.py:245-259) returns `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy(... decoder=partial(self.decode_payload, ...))` as the FIRST strategy, with no FilterStep upstream; the Kafka processor only submits KafkaPayload messages to the first step, and FilteredPayload is only emitted by filter steps. The path the comment describes is unreachable, and even then queue_consumer.py:317-325 completes the offset. A guard for an unreachable state is FP none.

I retain TP: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:586–589 wraps the strategy in DlqStaleMessagesStrategyFactoryWrapper when stale_threshold_sec is set. That wrapper forwards Message(Value(FILTERED_PAYLOAD, ...)) downstream from src/sentry/consumers/dlq.py:136–138, making the decoder assertion reachable. The new queue strategy consequently logs an exception; its fallback only completes BrokerValue offsets, so it does not complete this wrapper-generated message. The claim that no upstream filter can exist overlooks this consumer-level wrapper.

Concede. I missed the consumer-level wrapper: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:586-589 wraps every strategy factory in DlqStaleMessagesStrategyFactoryWrapper when stale_threshold_sec is set, and its poll submits `Message(Value(FILTERED_PAYLOAD, self.offsets_to_forward))` downstream (dlq.py:136-138). That reaches SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit, where `result = self.decoder(message.payload)` (queue_consumer.py:295) hits the decode_payload assertion (result_consumer.py:188), logs `Error submitting message to queue` (:318), and the fallback only completes BrokerValue offsets (:319), so the stale-skip offsets carried by that filtered message are dropped. Reachable, PR-introduced: TP none, medium (misleading error log plus lost commit of filtered offsets in a configuration-dependent path).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Untrusted SDK-controlled end_timestamp_precise is used verbatim as the ZSET score driving ZPOPMIN eviction. WHY: An attacker can send far-future timestamps to pin their spans and force eviction of legitimate spans in the same segment, biasing sampling/storage. HOW: Validate/clamp the score server-side instead of trusting client time.

hist.text: buffer.py:197-199 scores each span by its end_timestamp_precise, but the ZSET key is per project and trace (span-buf:s:{project:trace}:...), so a sender can only reorder eviction within its own trace; there is no cross-tenant or meaningful security impact.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:134-141 copies end_timestamp_precise from the incoming payload without validation, and src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197-199 uses it directly as the score. The newly added ZPOPMIN at src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62-63 therefore preferentially retains future-dated injected spans and evicts legitimate lower-scored spans when the same segment exceeds 1,000 members.

Keep FP none. Eviction by end timestamp is the PR's intended policy (add-buffer.lua:62-63 `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`), and the set is scoped per project and trace (buffer.py:196 `set_key = f"span-buf:s:{{{project_and_trace}}}:{parent_span_id}"`). Exploiting it needs injecting >1000 spans into a specific trace of the same project, which already lets the sender pollute that trace regardless of scores; no cross-tenant effect and no new security boundary crossed. Severity medium: telemetry of one segment only.

Changed to FP. buffer.py uses the supplied timestamp for retention ordering, but the affected set is scoped to one project's trace segment, and flushing uses server-side now plus a timeout. The base already allowed a sender injecting enough spans into that segment to make the entire segment exceed max_segment_spans and be discarded. The comment therefore does not establish a new security weakness beyond the sender's existing ability to poison that segment.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Every span insert runs up to two ZUNIONSTORE full copies of the up-to-1000-member set plus ZCARD/ZPOPMIN. WHY: Building a segment span-by-span copies O(N) per insert, i.e. O(N^2) total per segment and O(B*N) per batch in the ingest hot path. HOW: Merge once per batch or skip union when keys are already joined.

hist.text: add-buffer.lua:46-55 still merges at most two sets per insert as before; the PR only swaps sunionstore for zunionstore, which the base already ran on every insert, so the O(N) copy per insert is pre-existing and not introduced here.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:192-199 groups spans and inserts each subsegment together before executing the per-span scripts. Both unions are conditional on nonempty source sets and immediately unlink those sources (src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:46-54), so subsequent spans already joined do not repeatedly copy the set as claimed; the base also used full-set unions under the same conditions.

Keep FP none, not hallucination. The description is accurate: 'up to two ZUNIONSTORE' per insert (add-buffer.lua:46-55) and, when a segment's spans arrive in separate batches, each insert merges the 1-span parent_key into the N-member set_key, an O(N) copy, so O(N^2) per segment is real. What makes it FP is that the base did the same: the diff only swaps `sunionstore set_key, set_key, span_key` for `zunionstore set_key, 2, set_key, span_key` under the same conditions. Correct facts about pre-existing complexity -> FP none, as your own last sentence also notes.

Changed the subclass from hallucination to none. Separate batches can recreate a source set and repeatedly merge it into the growing destination, so conditional unions and unlinking do not rule out the described quadratic copying. The base performs SUNIONSTORE under the same conditions; the PR replaces it with ZUNIONSTORE, so the reported repeated full-set merging is pre-existing.
